sources.entry: Lumela - Cross-platform screenshot tool that blurs emails, card numbers, IPs and API keys with on-device OCR, then beautifies the shot. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/tw4/lumela) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon]

summary.one_liner: Lumela is a free, open-source screenshot tool for Windows, macOS and Linux that beautifies captures, annotates them, and auto-blurs emails, card numbers, IP addresses and API keys using on-device OCR.
summary.what_it_does: Lumela captures areas, single windows, or the full screen, with global shortcuts, a tray menu and multi-monitor support. It also accepts images opened from a file, the clipboard, or drag and drop. Captures can be beautified with an automatic background from the edge colour, gradients, solid colours, a custom image or wallpaper, plus padding, corner radius, and shadow. Aspect-ratio presets include social media sizes for X/Twitter, Instagram, LinkedIn, Facebook and YouTube. The annotation tools cover arrows, text, shapes, highlights and numbered steps, with undo/redo. Redaction offers pixelate, blur or solid boxes, and an Auto redact button finds emails, credit card numbers, IP addresses and API keys. Text recognition runs on the device so the user can select and copy words from an image, and export supports copy, save, PNG/JPEG, and drag-and-drop.
use_cases: blur sensitive info before sharing a screenshot
make screenshots look polished for social media or docs
annotate a screenshot with arrows and numbered steps
extract text from an image on my computer
capture a window or area of the screen with a shortcut
create presentation or post-ready images with a background
how_to_run: brew trust tw4/tap && brew install --cask tw4/tap/lumela (macOS, Homebrew)
git clone the repository and cd lumela
npm run tauri dev (run in development mode)
stack: Tesseract OCR (on Linux, installed separately or via .deb)
notable: Auto redact finds emails, card numbers, IPs and API keys in one click
OCR and redaction run on the device; no uploads, accounts or telemetry
Same editor and features on Windows, macOS and Linux
Small installers (about 4 MB Windows, 12 MB macOS per README)
Translated UI in multiple languages, with English and Turkish listed as the built-in languages
caveats: Installers are not code-signed yet, so the OS warns on first launch
Linux text recognition needs tesseract-ocr installed separately when using the AppImage
The only network request is the update check against the repository's releases
winget package is still under review
